title: Cronjob
subtitle: Schedule recurring SQL in a live DuckDB process.
intro: Register SQL with a six-field cron expression, inspect jobs and cancel by ID. The scheduler lives inside the DuckDB process, making it useful for short-lived local automation.

reference.name: cron(sql, schedule)
reference.description: Register a query; returns the job ID as VARCHAR.

reference.name: cron_jobs()
reference.description: Table function listing scheduled jobs and their status.

reference.name: cron_delete(job_id)
reference.description: Cancel a job using the ID returned by cron.

reference.name: second minute hour day month weekday
reference.description: Six fields: seconds come first, unlike five-field system cron.
Every five minutes, at second zero.
Daily at 02:00:00 in the scheduler environment.

notes.title: Keep the process alive
notes.body: The scheduler stops when DuckDB exits. Register jobs again after a restart; this is not a persistent system service or a replacement for an external orchestrator.

notes.title: Keep and use the returned ID
notes.body: Do not assume a job will always be task_0. Store the returned identifier and use it for cancellation. A successful registration does not establish that the scheduled SQL will succeed.

examples.title: Register a job
examples.caption: The example retains the actual ID so cancellation remains reliable.

examples.title: Inspect jobs
examples.caption: Review schedule and status while the same DuckDB process remains running.

examples.title: Cancel the registered job
examples.sql:
SELECT cron_delete(job_id) AS removed
FROM scheduled;
examples.caption: Cancel the example job when finished; no future execution remains scheduled.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cron_jobs() j JOIN scheduled s USING (job_id)) THEN true ELSE error('scheduled job was not removed') END;
